_what: What Damon has taught the cut. The cut prompt reads `rules` as {learned}, and they outrank its own rules. A rule is here because he SAID it as a rule, or because the same change was seen twice (prompts/stage-9-learn). `observations` are single changes — kept, not yet binding.

rules.rule: When there is a hook headline, it is on screen from the very first frame. It never fades or slides in.
rules.his_words: Whenever you have the hook-headline combo going on, that headline should begin at the beginning as well. Don't have it fade in; it should be at the start.

rules.rule: Never rebuild or re-voice talking A-roll in the edit. It is already good; the edit only puts B-roll on top of it, with its own sound kept so the lips match.
rules.his_words: you didn't even regenerate the A-roll. It was already good. It was just more about putting B-roll on top of it.

observations.saw: On the pigment hook he wanted the scroll stopper to run the length of the opening hook line — about four seconds — then cut to the rest of the A-roll, with a second B-roll over 'is why the sunscreen hasn't worked'. The model's first cut ran the stopper over the whole sentence and dropped the second clip.
observations.points_to: The scroll stopper covers the opening clause of the hook, not the whole sentence, and leaves room for the next B-roll.

observations.saw: He flagged that the headline has no safe zone against where her face sits in the frame. To be talked through later.
observations.points_to: Text placement should know where the face is.
